## GOAL ALIGNMENT
Part II:  Team Goals
HOW DO WE KNOW IF WE ARE SUCCESSFUL?  The following are a set of shared goals that align with our individual aims and that we can evaluate and metric over time to determine whether we are meeting our success criteria.

## (2) Project Objectives and Outcomes
- What is the main objective that we should try to achieve together and that would get you a long way toward meeting the challenge?
- Potential categories:  improved revenue, profitability, capabilities, customer intimacy, future optionality, culture, sustainability, cost structure, etc.
- At the end of this project, what would success look like?
- What are the greatest concerns, risks or jeopardies to our joint success in your mind?

## GOAL ALIGNMENT
Part I:  Individual Motivations, Strengths & Development Goals
WHO ARE WE AS A TEAM? Team exercise:  Discuss each member’s prior work experience, professional goals, and the core areas where you each hope to evolve as a leader.
Part II:  Team Goals
HOW DO WE KNOW IF WE ARE SUCCESSFUL?  Team exercise:  Based on your individual motivations, work together to develop your team’s goals while ensuring they align with your individual aims. Does each team member fully understand them and believe in them?  Are team members energized by them?  How will the team know if you’ve achieved these goals?  What impact will your team have if you achieve success?  What milestones need to be hit at what times to get there?
NOTE: Team goals should be challenging, consequential, and measurable.

## (5) Organization & Performance
- Who is the lead sponsor for this work?
- What are the key stakeholder groups who will need to be involved and consulted along the way?
- Is this organization going through any major internal transitions at present (e.g., of leadership, organizational structure, culture)?

answer:
The following are a set of shared goals that align with individual aims and can be evaluated and measured over time to determine success [S2]. Team goals should be challenging, consequential, and measurable [S4].

For the client, potential categories for objectives include improved revenue, profitability, capabilities, customer intimacy, future optionality, culture, sustainability, and cost structure, among others [S3].

For the team, team goals should be developed based on individual motivations while ensuring they align with individual aims [S4]. The team should also determine how they will know if they have achieved these goals [S4].
